transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2027-08-22
Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes
Fireflies meeting id: ff-20270822-lyonesse-01
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SA), Marcel (Lyonesse Head Sec), Ellen (Compliance), Ravi (Cloud), Jenna (Audit)

Summary:
Quick posture review for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 readiness, walk through trust access to reports, RBAC/SSO expectations, KMS/encryption model, and evidence onboarding plan. Agree next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Reports & Trust Center access (who gets what)
- Control mapping (Lyonesse controls -> Redwood artifacts)
- RBAC / SSO (SAML / OIDC details) and delegated admin model
- Audit logs, retention windows, and exportability
- Encryption / KMS options (BYOK, Redwood-managed, HSM)
- Data residency and private deployment considerations

Action items (also in metadata): see action_items field

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Sophie (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, can folks hear me?
[00:08] Marcel (Lyonesse): Yep, loud and clear. Good to see you all.
[00:12] Sophie: Great. Intro—I'm Sophie, AE on the account. With me are Daniel, our SE, and Priya on solutions. Today's goal is a posture orientation — show the artifacts we can share, discuss RBAC/SSO and KMS options, and map controls so your audit team knows what evidence we can provide.
[00:32] Daniel (Redwood SE): Hi all. I'll jump into the tech bits and then we can go control-by-control. Quick note, some of our doc names in the trust center are a little different than the way customers refer to them — so if something sounds off just call it out.
[01:05] Ellen (Compliance): Thanks. For us the big things are: access to SOC 2 Type II report, ISO scope statement, proof of encryption at rest and key custody, plus audit logs for model inputs/outputs and admin config changes.
[01:24] Priya (Redwood SA): Totally. We have a dedicated trust center bundle: SOC2 Type II summary (redacted), ISO27001 certificate and scope, and a controls matrix that ties Redwood policies to common frameworks. We'll point you to the exact URLs and also can give short-lived S3-style access if needed for your auditors.
[01:46] Marcel: Short-lived access sounds good — our internal rule is no more than 90 days for external auditor links. Can Redwood support that?
[01:54] Sophie: Yes, we can generate expiring links. We usually do a signed URL flow and can set TTLs to match your policy. We'll confirm acceptable TTLs in the follow-up.
[02:10] Ravi (Cloud): On the infra side, we need to understand log shipping — specifically what events are captured, retention, and whether logs include tokenized request IDs or full payloads. For privacy we can't have full PII in logs.
[02:32] Daniel: Good question. We capture admin events, model rollouts, config changes, and request metadata. By default payloads are not stored in plaintext in long-term logs; we have configurable redaction and tokenization for request/response content. There's also an option for per-customer prefix/KV cache where the request bodies are not persisted beyond ephemeral caches.
[02:58] Jenna (Audit Lead): When you say 'tokenization' — is that implemented in the platform or does the customer need to pre-process? We need to show auditors the mechanism.
[03:08] Priya: It's platform-level. We can enable redaction rules at the route level — regex-based — and we also offer a client-side SDK that can mask before transport. For the audit, we'll provide a diagram and the policy name used for your tenant.
[03:32] Ellen: Great. Next, RBAC and SSO — we use Okta and sometimes Azure AD. We need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for groups. What's Redwood's support look like?
[03:45] Daniel: We support SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning. Admin roles are mapped to RBAC roles in the console; you can set route-level permissions so devs don't see billing or trust artifacts. We'll share the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint details.
[04:10] Marcel: Do you support delegated admin? We have central security but want product teams to manage their own models.
[04:18] Sophie: Yes, we support org-level roles: Org Admin, Security Admin (can see trust center), Workspace Admin, Dev, Read-only. You can give Security Admin the ability to download reports but restrict product teams.
[04:36] Ravi: On KMS — our policy requires BYOK for production PII workloads. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed keys?
[04:47] Daniel: Yes. We support three modes: Redwood-managed keys (default), BYOK via KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault), and HSM integration for FIPS/HSM-backed keys. For BYOK we'll show the exchange flow and rotation patterns.
[05:06] Priya: Small note — there's also an option for a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) if you need full network control; that comes with a slightly different evidence set and some additional controls around key custody.
[05:25] Marcel: We're exploring private deployment for a subset of workloads. Can you outline the differences on audit evidence and access?
[05:33] Sophie: Sure — with private deployment, you'll get the platform runtime within your VPC and Redwood provides a private control plane. Evidence we provide will highlight the deployment mode, and for certain logs we may point to logs in your account rather than ours. We'll also document the network peering and access model in the control map.
[05:56] Jenna: For auditors, they want to see the separation of duties and exactly where logs live. If logs live in Lyonesse's cloud, that's easier for us.
[06:06] Daniel: Agreed. We'll create a 'log lineage' diagram showing which artifacts are stored in Redwood, which are pushed to your log sink, and where retention is enforced.
[06:22] Ellen: Back to SOC2 — we need to know the period covered by the Type II report and the specific controls tested. Does Redwood provide a mapping table to SOC2 CC categories?
[06:34] Priya: Yes, the controls matrix maps Redwood doc artifacts to SOC 2 CC criteria and also to ISO clauses. We'll attach that and highlight which controls are in-scope for hosted vs private deployments.
[06:46] Marcel: Ok. Are there any gaps you commonly see when customers try to map to their control set?
[06:54] Daniel: The common areas are: evidence for operator access reviews, key rotation proof (customers want rotation timestamps), and detailed admin audit trails for config changes. Those are straightforward but need explicit processes — we can show a sample runbook.
[07:14] Sophie: We'll also show the 'evidence export' feature — it compiles a zip with logs, configuration snapshots, IAM role change history across the selected period. It's redacted by default but can be configured per-request for auditors.
[07:36] Ravi: About encryption at rest — customers often ask whether embeddings are treated as first-class sensitive data. How does Redwood classify model outputs/embeddings?
[07:47] Priya: We treat embedding vectors as data; classification as sensitive depends on your policy. We offer optional deterministic hashing on embedding storage and provide the option to disable long-term persistence for embeddings. We'll call that out in the evidence docs.
[08:05] Ellen: Data residency — Lyonesse must keep certain records in EU region. Does Redwood provide region pinning for data and logs?
[08:14] Daniel: Yes — you can pin routes and models to regions. Observability and logs can be configured to live in a specific region and we will document the residency in the trust report for those routes.
[08:30] Marcel: For the trust center links, we need role-based visibility — only Security and Audit should see raw artifacts. Will the trust center respect SCIM group mapping?
[08:40] Sophie: Yes, trust center respects groups mapped via SCIM and SAML attributes. We'll provide a sample group policy that only surfaces full artifacts to Security Admins and gives summary metadata to Product Admins.
[09:00] Jenna: On evidence handoff — we prefer short-lived download links plus an audit trail of downloads. Is that in place?
[09:08] Daniel: Yes, downloads are logged with actor, timestamp, and evidence id. We can optionally include IP addresses for each access.
[09:18] Ellen: About automated control attestations — does Redwood have any built-in attestations or automated checks we can pull periodically?
[09:26] Priya: We have periodic self-checks and can export attestation logs for availability and patching. For deeper attestations (change control audits) we can produce a CSV of change requests and approvals within the covered period.
[09:45] Marcel: Next, can we drill into KMS exchange? Walk me through a BYOK key lifecycle.
[09:51] Daniel: Sure — step one: customer creates a key in their KMS (or HSM) and sets an IAM policy allowing Redwood's service principal to use Encrypt/Decrypt for the key. Step two: we register the key id to your tenant, and then the runtime uses the key to wrap data keys. We only store wrapped data keys; the plaintext key material remains in your KMS. Rotation is handled by you or via scheduled rotation policies, and we record rotation timestamps in the audit logs.
[10:28] Ravi: Will Redwood ever have the ability to export the plaintext?
[10:31] Daniel: No — in BYOK mode we never have access to plaintext key material. For Redwood-managed keys we do have access to the managed key but access is audited and restricted.
[10:44] Jenna: For the auditors, we need a statement of 'no plaintext access' for BYOK mode. Can Redwood provide that in writing?
[10:51] Priya: Yes, we can provide a formal note describing the BYOK guarantee and the mechanisms that enforce it. We'll include it in the trust bundle.
[11:08] Marcel: There was mention of 'KV cash' earlier — what exactly is that?
[11:12] Sophie: Sorry, that was me misspeaking — KV cache. It's the per-request prefix cache used for low-latency generation. Important for us: we can configure it to avoid long-term persistence for sensitive prefixes.
[11:30] Jenna: For compliance, we also need to demonstrate periodic access reviews. How does Redwood support scheduled reviews of admin roles?
[11:38] Daniel: We have a scheduled admin-review workflow that exports current role assignments and last sign-in timestamps; you can configure a 90-day review cadence and we will produce the export for auditors.
[11:52] Ellen: Do you integrate with our HR system for automated de-provisioning?
[11:57] Sophie: Through SCIM, yes — if your HR feeds into Okta/AD and SCIM syncs groups, de-provisioning happens automatically. We'll outline recommended SCIM attribute mappings.
[12:12] Marcel: Any constraints on SAML attributes? We need certain claims for our tooling.
[12:18] Priya: We support custom SAML attributes; typical ones are email, groups, orgUnit. We'll exchange metadata and map to roles.
[12:28] Ravi: Quick question on logs — is there a way to slice logs by model version and by route? We need per-model forensic capability.
[12:36] Daniel: Yes, logs include model_version and route_id metadata. You can query by those fields in the log export or via the console.
[12:46] Ellen: For evidence, auditors may request role change history for the last 12 months. Is that retained?
[12:52] Priya: By default we retain admin audit trails for 12 months; retention policy is configurable up to customer SLA — we can discuss longer retention for enterprise plans.
[13:06] Marcel: Let's talk about the controls mapping exercise — I want to understand how you annotate your artifacts to make it easy for auditors.
[13:15] Sophie: We tag artifacts with control ids and include a short narrative plus where the evidence resides. For example, control "CC6.4" would be linked to the admin-review export and a dated snapshot. We'll share a sample control mapping spreadsheet.
[13:34] Jenna: Could you show an example mapping for encryption controls?
[13:38] Priya: Example: CC5.2 (encryption at rest) -> Artifact: KMS key policy + audit log of rotation + storage config screenshot. Location: trust center / evidence export.
[13:54] Ravi: For private deployments, is the artifact still in the trust center or do we host it?
[13:59] Daniel: Usually for private deployments sensitive artifacts are hosted in your account; we reference them in the control map and include guidance on how to show the auditor.
[14:12] Marcel: What about penetration test reports — do you share a redacted pentest?
[14:18] Priya: Yes, we share a redacted pen-test summary and remediation timeline. Full internal reports are redacted, but we can provide what auditors need.
[14:30] Ellen: Any known open issues that typically take time in audits?
[14:35] Daniel: The usual friction points are: aligning customer rotation policies with platform rotation (timing), proving end-to-end key custody for BYOK scenarios, and getting network flow diagrams approved. Those are mostly documentation and configuration rather than product gaps.
[14:54] Sophie: We're going to upload a 'starter kit' for Lyonesse: sample control mapping spreadsheet, SAML/SCIM metadata templates, KMS BYOK runbook, and evidence export instructions.
[15:08] Marcel: That would be very helpful. Also, can you confirm the retention windows for logs in hosted? Our policy needs 2 years for certain logs.
[15:17] Daniel: Hosted default is 12 months, configurable to 24 months on enterprise contracts. We'll include retention pricing in the follow-up.
[15:30] Jenna: For auditors to reproduce findings, they like snapshots with timestamps. How granular are the snapshots?
[15:37] Priya: Our snapshots capture config state and relevant logs across a daily snapshot; we can produce point-in-time snapshots for any audit window requested.
[15:48] Ellen: If we go with a hybrid model (hosted for dev, private for prod) how do you handle canonical evidence?
[15:56] Sophie: We'll produce a combined control map indicating which artifacts are in your account vs Redwood's. We'll also flag evidence that is generated by Rhino — uh, Redwood — sorry, slip — that lives in our system versus artifacts you host.
[16:19] Marcel: On access logs — do you provide signed timestamps as proof?
[16:23] Daniel: We provide immutable log exports with checksums and can provide a signed manifest on request for the exported bundle.
[16:33] Ravi: A question on model drift and quality monitoring — not strictly security but can matter for some regs. Are those metrics part of the evidence set?
[16:41] Priya: We have quality monitoring and regression alerts; we can export evaluation runs and timestamps showing that monitoring was active.
[16:52] Marcel: Are there any legal agreements we should prepare for BYOK/HSM access?
[16:58] Sophie: Typically it's an addendum to the data processing agreement clarifying key ownership and KMS obligations. We'll share a redlined example.
[17:10] Jenna: For SOC2 coverage dates, when was Redwood's last audit?
[17:16] Priya: Our last Type II period ended June 30, 2027. We'll share the summary PDF and the tested control list.
[17:25] Marcel: Any outstanding open findings?
[17:28] Daniel: We had a minor finding around one patch window last year; remediation was completed and documented. We'll include the remediation memo in the package.
[17:41] Ellen: For the control mapping session next week, can we invite an internal Lyonesse engineer to walk through their current evidence repo?
[17:48] Sophie: Absolutely — that would speed things up.
[17:52] Ravi: On the technical side, can Daniel show a short log export demo?
[17:56] Daniel: Yep I can do a 8–10 minute demo. Should I share my screen now?
[18:02] Marcel: Go for it.
[18:05] [Screen share starts — brief pause]
[18:20] Daniel: I'm in the console. Here is the evidence export UI — select the date range, routes, model versions. You can toggle redaction rules. Note the 'Export manifest' checkbox which adds checksums.
[18:44] Jenna: That manifest looks useful. Can you show the admin audit timeline?
[18:51] Daniel: Sure — here is the admin timeline — filterable by actor, action, and date. You can download CSV.
[19:12] Sophie: Quick annotation — you'll see some names are service principals; we'll supply a mapping doc so auditors can map those to functions.
[19:26] Ellen: About export storage — where does the exported zip land?
[19:31] Daniel: Exports can land in a short-lived S3 link, or if you prefer we can push to your S3/GCP bucket via cross-account role.
[19:42] Ravi: We'll likely prefer cross-account push for high-sensitivity artifacts.
[19:45] Sophie: Noted. We'll include steps for the cross-account role.
[19:54] Marcel: Any specific network requirements for log push?
[19:58] Daniel: It uses standard outbound HTTPS. For private deployments we do VPC peering or private link. We'll capture exact ports and egress ranges in the tech appendix.
[20:12] Jenna: Can we talk about retention policy enforcement? For a 24-month retention, will Redwood incur additional costs or is that part of enterprise?
[20:20] Daniel: 24-month retention is an enterprise feature with incremental storage costs. We'll include pricing options.
[20:34] Ellen: For ISO27001, auditors want an inventory of assets in scope. Can Redwood produce an asset inventory for Lyonesse's tenant?
[20:41] Priya: We can produce a tenant-scoped inventory showing services used, model versions, and infra components that are in-scope.
[20:53] Marcel: Fantastic. Any concerns about data residency and cross-border transfers we should flag?
[20:59] Daniel: If we host anything outside your pinned region that could be a compliance issue — but we support strict region pinning. We'll validate your routes to ensure everything is region-aligned.
[21:15] Sophie: Quick housekeeping: we'll send the trust center links as protected docs, and Daniel will prepare the KMS diagram + demo artifacts. Priya will prepare the control mapping template.
[21:28] Marcel: Who will be our day-to-day SE contact for technical follow-ups?
[21:33] Sophie: Daniel will be primary, with Priya as backup for architecture questions.
[21:39] Jenna: On the auditor walkthrough — we want Redwood to attend a 30-minute call with our auditor to show the evidence export. Can you do that?
[21:47] Daniel: Yes, we can. We'll coordinate scheduling after we send the artifact links.
[21:54] Ellen: Are there any redactions we should expect in the SOC2 summary?
[21:58] Priya: We redact internal IPs and third-party identifiers; we keep the scope and control descriptions intact.
[22:08] Marcel: Ok let's set a tentative follow-up: control mapping workshop next Tuesday 14:00 UTC?
[22:15] Sophie: Works for us, I'll send an invite.
[22:19] Ravi: A couple of quick clarifications before wrap: 1) Will the KMS runbook include the exact IAM policy snippets? 2) Will the admin export include IP and user-agent?
[22:29] Daniel: Yes and yes. We'll include example IAM JSON and the admin export includes IP+UA by default.
[22:42] Jenna: For the evidence handoff, please include a short checklist our auditors can use to validate each artifact.
[22:48] Priya: We'll include a checklist template.
[22:53] Sophie: Great. Anything else?
[22:56] Marcel: One last thing — can you include a short statement on breach notification timelines and process?
[23:02] Priya: We have a defined incident response SLA — we notify customers within 48 hours for confirmed incidents and provide a timeline of remediation. We'll include the IR playbook excerpt.
[23:18] Ellen: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[23:22] Sophie: Thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts and set the control mapping workshop.
[23:27] [Meeting recap and quick readout]
[23:30] Sophie: Recap: 1) Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts & control mapping template. 2) Daniel to deliver KMS diagram and a log-export demo recording. 3) Lyonesse to share network diagram and list of control owners. 4) Schedule next week control mapping workshop.
[23:58] Marcel: Confirmed. Thanks.
[24:02] [Call ends]

Notes on transcription: minimal noise reduction applied, intermittent speaker attribution errors (occasionally 'Sophie' labelled as 'Speaker 1' in a couple of segments). Some jargon mis-heard ('KV cache' as 'KV cash') but clarified during call.
